options: Knowing which kinds of data an organisation has, with monetary value
Knowing system details, databases, tables and columns mapped to business requirements
A consolidation of Data Asset and Data Catalogue information with additional details such as origin, ownership and frequency of change
A list of passwords for social media applications
The process of generating synthetic customer data
questions.explanation: Data Inventory consolidates the information in Data Assets and Data Catalogue and adds details such as where data comes from, who generated it, when, and how often it changes.

questions.stem: Which concept is about knowing which kind of data an organisation has, together with its monetary value?
questions.explanation: Data Assets is about knowing what data the organisation holds and what monetary value it carries.

questions.stem: Which concept is about knowing system details, databases, tables and columns and mapping them to business requirements?
questions.explanation: Data Catalogue covers system details, databases, tables and columns and their mapping to business requirements.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed among the additional details captured in a Data Inventory?
options: Frequency of inserts, updates and deletes
Owners of source and target systems
The exchange rate used for data valuation
questions.explanation: Change frequency, licensing, system owners and security approaches are all inventory details; an exchange rate for valuation is not.

questions.stem: Which everyday example illustrates the idea of an inventory in *I Am Datapedia!*?
options: A Passwords Inventory kept safely for social media, Hotmail, Gmail and other accounts
questions.explanation: Keeping all one's passwords for the many applications and email services in one safe place is a Password Inventory, an everyday parallel to Data Inventory.

questions.stem: For which parties is Data Inventory described as a key input?
questions.explanation: Data inventory is one of the key inputs for regulatory bodies, compliance and auditors.

questions.stem: Which event made Data Inventory more important than ever, according to *I Am Datapedia!*?
options: The Covid-19 impact of 2019 to 2022, when working from home pushed reluctant organisations to the cloud
questions.explanation: During Covid-19, most of the world was forced to work from home and organisations that had resisted the cloud moved to it, making data inventory more important than ever.

questions.stem: Data Inventory is itself described as an example of what?
questions.explanation: The topic concludes with the statement that Data Inventory is also a Metadata.

questions.stem: As of May 2022, what proportion of organisations does *I Am Datapedia!* say have both on-premises and cloud presence?
questions.explanation: The author estimates that, if not 100%, then 99% or more of organisations have both on-premises and cloud presence, even if only through conferencing tools or WhatsApp.

questions.stem: Which pair of items both belong to the additional details in a Data Inventory?
questions.explanation: Transformation details and business rules are among the listed inventory items, along with data models, software lists, data sources and target systems.
